nodes.name: stylua.toml
nodes.summary: Stylua Lua formatter configuration with 160-column width, 2-space indent, single-quote preference, no call parentheses, and sorted requires.

nodes.name: init.lua
nodes.summary: Neovim configuration entry point. Requires the config submodules in load order (options, keymaps, autocmds, pack, plugins, load_lsp) and applies the shades-of-purple colorscheme at startup.

nodes.name: autocmds.lua
nodes.summary: Registers Neovim autocmds for filetype concealment, formatoptions cleanup, cursorline toggling per window, and relative/absolute line-number switching on focus/insert events.

nodes.name: keymaps.lua
nodes.summary: Comprehensive default keymap set covering search, window movement, line moving, diagnostics navigation, quickfix/location lists, and editor primitives. Defines local helpers open_url, searching_brave, and diagnostic_goto.

nodes.name: load_lsp.lua
nodes.summary: Configures vim.diagnostic virtual_text and severity signs, then binds the LspLensToggle leader mapping. Minimal LSP-adjacent setup loaded after plugins.

nodes.name: lsp.lua
nodes.summary: Fully commented-out legacy LSP configuration documenting vim.lsp.config setups for 20+ language servers (rust-analyzer, gopls, clangd, lua_ls, pyright, ruff, ts_ls, and more). Inactive in the current runtime; per-language configs now live in lua/plugins/lang/*.

nodes.name: options.lua
nodes.summary: Sets global Neovim options and globals: encoding, backup dir, leader key, root-detection spec, spell, backspace, conceallevel, and disabled providers. Wraps vim.keymap.set to force silent=true by default.

nodes.name: pack.lua

nodes.name: health.lua

nodes.name: check_version

nodes.name: check_external_reqs

nodes.name: check

layers.name: Bootstrap Layer
layers.description: Neovim entry point (init.lua) and health-check module (health.lua) that bootstrap the runtime, register plugins, and validate the environment at startup.

layers.name: Core Configuration Layer
layers.description: Editor options, keymaps, autocmds, LSP diagnostics, pack hooks, and legacy LSP reference, plus root-level tooling configuration (.luarc.json, .neoconf.json, stylua.toml, nvim-pack-lock.json) and user-facing documentation (README.md, KEYMAP.md, CONTRIBUTING.md).

layers.name: Plugin Layer
layers.description: All 88 vim.pack plugin modules under lua/plugins/ (including lua/plugins/lang/ language server configs), each registering a third-party Neovim plugin and its setup, with heavy cross-dependency coupling among themselves.

layers.name: Shared Utility Layer
layers.description: Cross-cutting Lua helpers (lua/utils/init.lua) that every other module depends on, acting as the foundation of the dependency hierarchy.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand the project's purpose, architecture, and how to get started. This single-title document outlines what the nvim-config Neovim configuration provides and serves as the roadmap for the tour ahead.

tour.title: Bootstrap Entry Point
tour.description: The Neovim configuration entry point. Requires the config submodules in load order (options, keymaps, autocmds, pack, plugins, load_lsp) and applies the shades-of-purple colorscheme at startup. This file gives you the bird's-eye view of the project's runtime structure and dependency hierarchy.
tour.languageLesson: Neovim's init.lua is the equivalent of .vimrc — it is loaded automatically at startup and orchestrates the entire configuration. The health.lua module follows the standard Neovim health check pattern, returning a table with check_version, check_external_reqs, and check functions that integrate with :checkhealth.

tour.title: Shared Utility Foundation
tour.description: The shared Lua helper module that every other module depends on, acting as the foundation of the dependency hierarchy. With 68 incoming edges from across the plugin layer, this module provides cross-cutting utilities (URL helpers, LSP attach hooks, filetype gating) that plugin specs call repeatedly rather than re-implementing.
tour.languageLesson: This module uses the Lua module pattern with a local M = {} table. The utils.gh helper constructs GitHub raw URLs from owner/repo/shorthand, a pattern repeated across dozens of plugin stubs — notice how the shared helper prevents URL string duplication across 80+ plugin files.

tour.title: Core Configuration Layer
tour.description: The foundational editor configuration: options.lua sets global options (encoding, backup dir, leader key, root-detection spec, spell, backspace, conceallevel) and wraps vim.keymap.set to force silent=true by default; keymaps.lua defines the comprehensive default keymap set covering search, window movement, diagnostics navigation, and editor primitives; autocmds.lua registers filetype concealment, formatoptions cleanup, cursorline toggling, and relative/absolute line-number switching.
tour.languageLesson: The keymap wrapper in options.lua demonstrates a common Lua pattern: a local function that captures default arguments via closure and delegates to vim.keymap.set, enforcing silent=true across the entire codebase without repeating the argument in every call.

tour.title: Plugin Loader
tour.description: The plugin loader that activates every top-level plugin spec in the directory. Globs lua/plugins/*.lua at startup and loadfile's each non-init spec file, stripping numeric load-order prefixes and guarding against double-loading via package.loaded. This is the gateway through which all 88 plugin modules flow into the runtime.
tour.languageLesson: The loader uses loadfile() rather than require() deliberately: numeric prefixes like 00-snacks.lua break Lua's module resolution (require looks for lua/plugins/00-snacks.lua which is an invalid identifier), but loadfile loads by path. The package.loaded guard prevents re-executing top-level vim.pack.add calls on every boot.

tour.title: Package Management & Build Hooks
tour.description: The pack.lua PackChanged autocmd hook runs post-install builds for telescope-fzf-native.nvim and LuaSnip, and triggers TSUpdate after nvim-treesitter install/update. This ensures that compiled dependencies are rebuilt whenever the plugin set changes, bridging the gap between vim.pack's install lifecycle and plugins that require native compilation.
tour.languageLesson: The nvim-pack-lock.json is a generated lock file pinning 82 bundled Neovim plugins with exact versions. It serves the same purpose as npm's package-lock.json or Cargo's Cargo.lock: reproducible installs across machines by recording the resolved versions of every dependency.

tour.title: First Plugin: Snacks.nvim
tour.description: The first-loaded plugin spec (00- prefix): registers folke/snacks.nvim via vim.pack.add, runs require('snacks').setup(), and defines the bulk of the <leader>s* picker, <leader>u* toggle, and <leader>g* git keymaps. Loaded first so other modules can depend on Snacks being available — it is the single most depended-upon plugin in the configuration.
tour.languageLesson: The 00- prefix is a deliberate load-order convention: by loading before all other plugins, Snacks.nvim's global state (pickers, git integration, util helpers) is available when later modules call require('snacks').setup() or snacks.util.lsp.on() — a form of implicit dependency ordering through file naming.

tour.title: Treesitter Foundation
tour.description: Configures nvim-treesitter with indent, highlight, and fold features, plus a FileType autocmd for lazy per-buffer setup across 25 languages. This is the syntactic backbone of the entire editor: it provides the parse trees that power syntax highlighting, code folding, textobjects, and incremental selection that nearly every other plugin builds upon.
tour.languageLesson: nvim-treesitter's incremental selection uses the parser's AST to select ranges of code at increasing granularity — from the current node up to the root. The FileType autocmd defers parser loading until a file is actually opened, keeping startup fast while supporting 25 languages on demand.

tour.title: Formatting & Linting System
tour.description: Conform.nvim registers a toggleable BufWritePre autocmd that calls conform.format on save, exposing M.format_on_save/M.toggle/M.is_on plus <leader>cf/<leader>cF keymaps. The language-specific modules (go.lua, lua.lua, python.lua, rust.lua, typescript.lua) wire per-language formatters and linters into Conform and nvim-lint, creating a unified auto-format pipeline that works across all supported languages.
tour.languageLesson: The language modules follow a consistent pattern: each pulls its formatter (gofumpt, stylua, ruff, rustfmt) into conform.formatters and its linter (golangci-lint, ruff, clippy) into nvim-lint.linters_by_ft — demonstrating how a shared plugin abstraction (Conform for formatting, nvim-lint for linting) avoids per-plugin configuration duplication.

tour.title: Language Module Barrel
tour.description: The language-module barrel that requires each config.lang.* module (angular through zig) in a single require chain. Each sub-module configures treesitter parsers, LSP servers, formatters, and linters for its language family — this barrel is the single point through which all language support flows into the runtime.
tour.languageLesson: This is a Lua barrel file: a single init file that requires every language module in sequence. The pattern is identical to a JavaScript barrel index.ts — a one-line-per-language require chain that centralizes language configuration and makes it easy to add or remove a language by editing one file.

tour.title: Statusline & UI Integration
tour.description: Configures lualine statusline with custom root-directory component, pretty-path component, diagnostics/git/diff sections, and noice/dap/lazy extension integrations. The statusline pulls information from multiple plugins (diagnostics from vim.diagnostic, git from gitsigns, search from noice) and composes them into a single cohesive status bar.
tour.languageLesson: Lualine's extension system is a form of composition: rather than hardcoding statusline sections, the config registers extensions for noice (command-line messages), dap (debugger state), and lazy (plugin manager status). Each extension is a table of sections that lualine renders conditionally — a plug-and-play statusline architecture.

tour.title: LSP Tooling & Diagnostics
tour.description: load_lsp.lua configures vim.diagnostic virtual_text and severity signs, then binds the LspLensToggle leader mapping. The legacy lsp.lua file contains fully commented-out LSP configuration documenting vim.lsp.config setups for 20+ language servers — it is inactive in the current runtime, with per-language configs now living in lua/plugins/lang/*. This layer bridges the gap between the LSP servers configured in the language modules and the user-facing diagnostic display.
tour.languageLesson: The commented-out lsp.lua serves as a historical artifact and reference: it documents the pre-plugin LSP setup pattern (vim.lsp.config per server) that has been replaced by the per-language module approach. This is a common pattern in evolving codebases — the old approach is preserved as documentation rather than deleted, so newcomers can understand what changed and why.

tour.title: Plugin Manager UI
tour.description: An interactive vim.pack plugin manager UI as a floating window with refresh, update, uninstall, and key navigation. This is the user-facing tool for managing the plugin set at runtime — it wraps vim.pack's API behind a friendly floating-window interface with commit loading, update status display, and one-key-per-plugin navigation.
tour.languageLesson: The pack_float module demonstrates the NUI (Native UI) pattern in Neovim: it builds a floating window buffer with virtual text for plugin status, then uses vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd to refresh content on BufEnter and TermClose events. The 20+ functions (setup, set_plugins, build_content, load_commits, etc.) follow a clear separation between data fetching (async refresh_fetch) and UI rendering (set_lines).

tour.title: Developer Tooling Configuration
tour.description: Root-level tooling configuration: .luarc.json declares Neovim globals (vim, Snacks) and suppresses undefined-doc-name diagnostics for the Snacks plugin API; .neoconf.json enables the neodev library and lua_ls plugin for the Neovim Lua LSP workspace; stylua.toml configures the Stylua Lua formatter with 160-column width, 2-space indent, single-quote preference, and sorted requires. Together these files ensure the configuration codebase itself is properly linted, formatted, and type-checked.

tour.title: Documentation & Contribution Guide
tour.description: KEYMAP.md is a comprehensive keymap reference organized into 20 sections covering movement, windows, editing, LSP, buffers, Snacks pickers, git, terminal, and toggles — it documents the complete keybinding surface. CONTRIBUTING.md covers development setup, prerequisites (Neovim, Jujutsu), repository cloning, and running the config via nvim -u ./init.lua, providing the onboarding path for external contributors.
tour.languageLesson: KEYMAP.md's 20-section organization mirrors the layered architecture of the config itself: it groups keymaps by functional area (movement, windows, LSP, buffers) rather than by the file that defines them, making it useful as a user-facing reference regardless of which plugin module happens to own each binding.

project.name: nvim-pack
project.description: Neovim configuration managed by nvim-pack, bundling 97 Lua plugin modules and 4 config files (options, keymaps, autocmds, pack) into a modular runtime. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.
